land.text: the Captaincy General of Santo Domingo, eastern Hispaniola: the state 'succeeded the Captaincy General of Santo Domingo after independence was declared'

predecessors.note: No Cliopatria shape of its own; the Spanish Empire row is the nearest.

land.text: the eastern part of the island: 'On 9 February 1822, Boyer formally entered the capital city'

successors.note: The haiti dossier (am-08-a) records the same gain.

rulers.name: José Núñez de Cáceres
rulers.note: Declared independence on 1 December 1821 and received Boyer on 9 February 1822; the page gives no title.

correction.text: the eastern part of Hispaniola, the former Captaincy General of Santo Domingo, infobox area 54,442 km2

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row for 1821-1822. Infobox area 54,442 km2; the gazetteer resolves the Dominican Republic to 252 cells, about 63,700 km2 (ratio 1.17, within the factor of two). The shape is reduced in the ledger as Puerto Plata (13 December 1821), Dajabón (15 December), Santiago (29 December) and La Vega (4 January 1822) raise the Haitian flag.

region.text: eastern Hispaniola: 'independence was declared on 1 December 1821 by José Núñez de Cáceres'

ledger.note: 1 December 1821: Núñez de Cáceres declares the independence of Spanish Haiti at Santo Domingo. Infobox 'Ephemeral Independence: 1 December 1821'; the state's constitution 'declared it as a state of Gran Colombia'.

region.text: Puerto Plata, which raised the Haitian flag

ledger.note: 13 December 1821: Puerto Plata raises the Haitian flag. 'On 13 December 1821, Puerto Plata raised the Haitian flag.' The page names the town; the province is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Dajabón, which raised the Haitian flag

ledger.note: 15 December 1821: Dajabón raises the Haitian flag on the frontier with Haiti.

region.text: Santiago, which raised the Haitian flag

ledger.note: 29 December 1821: Santiago raises the Haitian flag.

region.text: La Vega, which raised the Haitian flag

ledger.note: 4 January 1822: La Vega raises the Haitian flag; 'the people began to raise the Haitian flag on public buildings and plazas.'

region.text: the rest of the island, with the capital: 'Boyer formally entered the capital city'

ledger.note: 9 February 1822: Boyer enters Santo Domingo. 'On 9 February 1822, Boyer formally entered the capital city, Santo Domingo', where Núñez de Cáceres received him; the island is united under Haiti.
February 1822: Spanish Haiti ends in the Haitian occupation. Infobox 'Haitian occupation: 9 February 1822'.

wars.name: Haitian occupation of Santo Domingo (1822)
wars.outcome: Haitian annexation without a battle: towns raise the Haitian flag from 13 December 1821 and Boyer enters Santo Domingo on 9 February 1822.
wars.note: The page records no fighting, so no contested zone is drawn.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary text for the frontier with Haiti; the island is shown as the former Captaincy General of Santo Domingo.

sources.title: Republic of Spanish Haiti
sources.note: Declaration 1 December 1821, infobox area 54,442 km2, Haitian flags raised 13 December 1821 to 4 January 1822, Boyer in Santo Domingo 9 February 1822.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row for this state. The haiti dossier (am-08-a) names it as counterpart of the 9 February 1822 gain (republic-of-spanish-haiti).
One page opened (budget 1-2). The page does not date the retreat of Spanish authority between Spain's 1809 reconquest and 1821 and gives no Gran Colombia reply; those are outside this dossier.
